digest.component_or_area: operator-attested evidence contract and plan-review gating
propositions: Operator-attested evidence currently validates the attestation event's provenance (change id / vote / timestamp) but not the measurement's context (environment, principal, privilege level), leaving escape routes via wrong-environment measurements or measurements taken under broader privilege than production.

Two real escapes occurred: bedrock caching measured in account 579718921998/us-east-2 but recorded as settled fact for account 896586841071/us-east-1, and live API calls made under bedrock:* identity used as proof of scoped bedrock:InvokeModel grant, both satisfying the current contract.

The fix extends the operator-attested contract with four required text fields (environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument) declared on an indented continuation line under the checkbox, forcing measurement context into the record where repo-grounded checks and human reviewers can find contradictions.

A deterministic (non-LLM) check validates presence, non-placeholder values, and enum membership of the four provenance fields, making no judgement about correctness; a tool-enabled AGENT-tier criterion then probes declared environment against in-repo IaC anchors and checks privilege_posture against the criterion's claim type.

The criterion ships advisory on first landing via .rebar/ project overlay, never blocking pre-contract tickets and only firing on plans that actually carry [operator-attested] tags, with corpus replay per ADR-0054 required before any promotion to blocking.

Six remaining acceptance criteria proving the AGENT criterion's runtime behaviour (contradiction detection on wrong environment, privilege-posture judgement, instrument-vs-authorization-claim rule, no-anchor fallback, contrast cases, FP rate calibration) are descoped to ticket 98df and not claimed as done here.
